name: devspace
description: Minimal Coding Agent Harness on MCP for ChatGPT, Claude, Hermes, Grok Bot, OpenClaw
readmeExcerpt:
DevSpace

Give ChatGPT, Claude, and Grok Bot your computer. Let any coding agent hand work to any other.

DevSpace is the agent-agnostic layer between the AI you talk to and the coding agents on your machine. It does two things: - **Connects MCP hosts to your machine.** ChatGPT, Claude, and proactive agents like Grok Bot, OpenClaw, and Hermes open a workspace, read and edit files, run your tests, and show you a review card of the diff — against your real checkout, through a tunnel you own. - **Lets agents delegate to each other.** Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Pi, Cursor, Copilot, and Grok Build run as subagents of whichever agent is in charge, using the CLIs and subscriptions you already have. Parallel writers get their own Git worktrees. Your agent stays the orchestrator: DevSpace never runs a hidden agent loop of its own. And there is no DevSpace service — everything runs locally with your credentials. ## Sponsors and Special Thanks

DevSpace is open to new sponsors. Get in touch to become one.

## Installation macOS, Linux, and WSL: ```bash curl -fsSL https://devspace.run/install | sh ``` Windows (DevSpace also needs Git Bash): ```powershell powershell -c "irm https://devspace.run/install.ps1 | iex" ``` The installer uses a compatible Node (`>=22.19 <27`) on your `PATH` or downloads Node 24 LTS for DevSpace alone, installs without `sudo`, and starts `devspace init`. Rerun it to update. If you manage Node yourself, `npm install -g @waishnav/devspace` followed by `devspace init` also works. `devspace init` asks where you will use DevSpace and which agents it may run as subagents. Each question can also be answered with a flag, so scripts and agents can set it up without prompts: ```bash devspace init --yes # subagents only devspace init --public-url https://your-tunnel.example.com --roots ~/work # also serve an MCP host ``` **Let your agent set itself up.** The **Copy prompt** button on [devspace.run](https://devspace.run) copies a prompt you can paste into Codex, Claude Code, or any agent with a shell. It installs, configures, and checks DevSpace without asking you anything. ## Use It from Your Coding Agents Subagents need no server, tunnel, or OAuth. Install the skill that teaches your agent the workflow, then delegate: ```bash devspace agents skill --install # Cursor: devspace agents skill --install cursor --project devspace agents run codex "Review the staged diff for correctness" devspace agents run pi "Check the staged diff for test gaps" devspace agents wait ``` - **Profiles** turn your "which model for which job" choices into named roles (`planner`, `reviewer`, …) as Markdown files you own. - **Worktrees** (`--worktree`) let agents edit in parallel without touching your checkout. - **Dynamic workflows** (experimental, `DEVSPACE_EXPERIMENTAL_WORKFLOWS=1`) let the orchestrator write a small, resumable script with `agent()`, `parallel()`, `pipeline()`, and `phase()` instead of prompting step by step. ## Use It from ChatGPT, Claude, and Other MCP Hosts Start a tunnel (Cloudflare Tunnel, ngrok, Pinggy, Tailscale Funnel, or your own HTTPS reverse proxy) to `http://127.0.0.1:7676`, run `devspace serve`, and add the public `/mcp` URL as a connector in your host: ```text https://your-tunnel-host.example.com/mcp ``` When the host connects, DevSpace opens an Owner password approval page. The password is stored in `~/.devspace/auth.json`; keep it private. The `/mcp` endpoint serves the 2026-07-28 protocol and older 2025-era clients without any configuration. Once connected, the host can open one of your allowed project folders as a workspace and: - read, write, and edit files, and search code - run shell commands for tests, builds, Git, and package scripts - use isolated Git worktrees for parallel sessions - follow project instructions from `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`, and discover your skills - show a change-review card at the end of a turn - delegate to your coding agents through the same `devspace agents` CLI > [!NOTE] > Using DevSpace as an MCP connector isn't against OpenAI's Usage Policies — it's > a standard custom App/connector setup, and writing or running code isn't a > restricted use case. But your account is governed by your usage, not by > DevSpace. Don't point it at anything that would violate your provider's terms. > Used normally, you're fine. (Based on OpenAI's Usage Policies and Service Terms > as of June 2026.) ## Mental Model DevSpace is remote access to selected local folders, plus a way for your agents to work together. You decide which roots an MCP host may open. Inside a workspace the host has powerful local capabilities, including shell execution, so treat a connected host like a trusted coding partner with access to your machine. Subagents run with your local user's authority and logins, scoped to the project they are started from. ## Platform Support DevSpace supports Linux, macOS, and Windows environments with a Bash-compatible shell. | Platform | Status | Notes | | ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | | Linux | Supported | Requires Node, npm, Git, and Bash. | | macOS | Supported | Requires Node, npm, Git, and Bash. | | Windows with Git Bash, WSL, MSYS2, or Cygwin Bash | Supported | Git Bash is the simplest native Windows setup. | | Windows PowerShell or `cmd.exe` only | Not supported yet | Install Git Bash or use WSL. | Run this to inspect your local setup: ```bash devspace doctor ``` ## Documentation Full documentation lives at [devspace.run/docs](https://devspace.run/docs): - [Quickstart](https://devspace.run/docs/quickstart) - [Connect ChatGPT, Claude, Grok Bot, and other MCP hosts](https://devspace.run/docs/connect/mcp-hosts) - [Use DevSpace from Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, and bots](https://devspace.run/docs/connect/coding-agents) - [Subagents](https://devspace.run/docs/orchestration/subagents) and [agent profiles](https://devspace.run/docs/orchestration/profiles) - [Dynamic workflows](https://devspace.run/docs/orchestration/dynamic-workflows) - [CLI reference](https://devspace.run/docs/reference/cli) and [configuration reference](https://devspace.run/docs/reference/configuration) - [Security model](https://devspace.run/docs/concepts/security) - [Troubleshooting](https://devspace.run/docs/reference/troubleshooting) ## Philosophy Every piece of software is becoming conversational, and every provider is racing to make _their_ agent the orchestrator. In practice, people already pick a different model and harness per task: one to plan, another to implement, a cheap one to explore, a second vendor to review. That matrix is personal, and it changes every few weeks. DevSpace keeps it yours. Whichever agent you talk to — ChatGPT, Claude, Grok Bot, or a coding agent in your terminal — can reach your machine and hand work to the others, through explicit, inspectable tools instead of one vendor's closed loop. ## Built by Waishnav I'm Waishnav. I like building opinionated products and tools, and DevSpace is one example. This year, I began my journey to build a one-person, multi-agent company capable of generating millions in revenue. If you want to follow the failures, wins, lessons, and everything in between, come hang out with me on [X](https://x.com/wshxnv). ## More from me

## Local Development For working on DevSpace itself: Install pnpm 11.25.0, the version pinned in `package.json`, with `npm install --global pnpm@11.25.0`, then: ```bash pnpm install --frozen-lockfile pnpm dev:seed pnpm dev pnpm typecheck pnpm test pnpm build pnpm start ``` `dev:seed` forks your normal DevSpace config and SQLite state into an ignored checkout-local `.devspace-dev/` directory so source builds and migrations do not modify your normal installation. Use `pnpm dev:reset` to discard that QA state and fork it again. See [DEVELOPMENT.md](DEVELOPMENT.md) for worktree switching, real-host QA, and database-migration workflows.

DevSpace

Give ChatGPT, Claude, and Grok Bot your computer. Let any coding agent hand work to any other.

DevSpace is the agent-agnostic layer between the AI you talk to and the coding agents on your machine. It does two things:

  • Connects MCP hosts to your machine. ChatGPT, Claude, and proactive agents like Grok Bot, OpenClaw, and Hermes open a workspace, read and edit files, run your tests, and show you a review card of the diff — against your real checkout, through a tunnel you own.
  • Lets agents delegate to each other. Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Pi, Cursor, Copilot, and Grok Build run as subagents of whichever agent is in charge, using the CLIs and subscriptions you already have. Parallel writers get their own Git worktrees.

Your agent stays the orchestrator: DevSpace never runs a hidden agent loop of its own. And there is no DevSpace service — everything runs locally with your credentials.

Sponsors and Special Thanks

DevSpace is open to new sponsors. Get in touch to become one.

Installation

macOS, Linux, and WSL:

curl -fsSL https://devspace.run/install | sh

Windows (DevSpace also needs Git Bash):

powershell -c "irm https://devspace.run/install.ps1 | iex"

The installer uses a compatible Node (>=22.19 <27) on your PATH or downloads Node 24 LTS for DevSpace alone, installs without sudo, and starts devspace init. Rerun it to update. If you manage Node yourself, npm install -g @waishnav/devspace followed by devspace init also works.

devspace init asks where you will use DevSpace and which agents it may run as subagents. Each question can also be answered with a flag, so scripts and agents can set it up without prompts:

devspace init --yes                                                      # subagents only
devspace init --public-url https://your-tunnel.example.com --roots ~/work # also serve an MCP host

Let your agent set itself up. The Copy prompt button on devspace.run copies a prompt you can paste into Codex, Claude Code, or any agent with a shell. It installs, configures, and checks DevSpace without asking you anything.

Use It from Your Coding Agents

Subagents need no server, tunnel, or OAuth. Install the skill that teaches your agent the workflow, then delegate:

devspace agents skill --install <claude-code|codex|opencode|agents>
# Cursor: devspace agents skill --install cursor --project

devspace agents run codex "Review the staged diff for correctness"
devspace agents run pi "Check the staged diff for test gaps"
devspace agents wait <id> <id>
  • Profiles turn your "which model for which job" choices into named roles (planner, reviewer, …) as Markdown files you own.
  • Worktrees (--worktree) let agents edit in parallel without touching your checkout.
  • Dynamic workflows (experimental, DEVSPACE_EXPERIMENTAL_WORKFLOWS=1) let the orchestrator write a small, resumable script with agent(), parallel(), pipeline(), and phase() instead of prompting step by step.

Use It from ChatGPT, Claude, and Other MCP Hosts

Start a tunnel (Cloudflare Tunnel, ngrok, Pinggy, Tailscale Funnel, or your own HTTPS reverse proxy) to http://127.0.0.1:7676, run devspace serve, and add the public /mcp URL as a connector in your host:

https://your-tunnel-host.example.com/mcp

When the host connects, DevSpace opens an Owner password approval page. The password is stored in ~/.devspace/auth.json; keep it private. The /mcp endpoint serves the 2026-07-28 protocol and older 2025-era clients without any configuration.

Once connected, the host can open one of your allowed project folders as a workspace and:

  • read, write, and edit files, and search code
  • run shell commands for tests, builds, Git, and package scripts
  • use isolated Git worktrees for parallel sessions
  • follow project instructions from AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, and discover your skills
  • show a change-review card at the end of a turn
  • delegate to your coding agents through the same devspace agents CLI

Note

Using DevSpace as an MCP connector isn't against OpenAI's Usage Policies — it's a standard custom App/connector setup, and writing or running code isn't a restricted use case. But your account is governed by your usage, not by DevSpace. Don't point it at anything that would violate your provider's terms. Used normally, you're fine. (Based on OpenAI's Usage Policies and Service Terms as of June 2026.)

Mental Model

DevSpace is remote access to selected local folders, plus a way for your agents to work together.

You decide which roots an MCP host may open. Inside a workspace the host has powerful local capabilities, including shell execution, so treat a connected host like a trusted coding partner with access to your machine. Subagents run with your local user's authority and logins, scoped to the project they are started from.

Platform Support

DevSpace supports Linux, macOS, and Windows environments with a Bash-compatible shell.

Platform Status Notes
Linux Supported Requires Node, npm, Git, and Bash.
macOS Supported Requires Node, npm, Git, and Bash.
Windows with Git Bash, WSL, MSYS2, or Cygwin Bash Supported Git Bash is the simplest native Windows setup.
Windows PowerShell or cmd.exe only Not supported yet Install Git Bash or use WSL.

Run this to inspect your local setup:

devspace doctor

Documentation

Full documentation lives at devspace.run/docs:

  • Quickstart
  • Connect ChatGPT, Claude, Grok Bot, and other MCP hosts
  • Use DevSpace from Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, and bots
  • Subagents and agent profiles
  • Dynamic workflows
  • CLI reference and configuration reference
  • Security model
  • Troubleshooting

Philosophy

Every piece of software is becoming conversational, and every provider is racing to make their agent the orchestrator.

In practice, people already pick a different model and harness per task: one to plan, another to implement, a cheap one to explore, a second vendor to review. That matrix is personal, and it changes every few weeks.

DevSpace keeps it yours. Whichever agent you talk to — ChatGPT, Claude, Grok Bot, or a coding agent in your terminal — can reach your machine and hand work to the others, through explicit, inspectable tools instead of one vendor's closed loop.

Built by Waishnav

releases.name: v1.1.1
releases.body:
DevSpace 1.1.1 lets `devspace init` run without prompts, so a coding agent, a script, or a fresh machine can set DevSpace up without anyone at the keyboard.

## Set up without prompts

`init` still asks its questions in a terminal. Now each flag answers one of them, `--yes` takes the defaults for the rest, and without a terminal `init` uses the defaults too.

```bash
devspace init --yes                                                      # subagents
devspace init --public-url https://your-tunnel.example.com --roots ~/work # also serve ChatGPT or Claude
```

- **`--providers codex,claude`** picks the subagents. It defaults to configured providers, else every detected one.
- **`--public-url`** sets your tunnel's origin, without `/mcp`. Setting one is what also serves an MCP host.
- **`--roots`** sets the project folders an MCP host may open. It's required with a public URL unless roots are already configured, so an MCP host never gets a guessed root.
- **`--json`** prints the result for scripts. It reports where the owner password is stored, never the password itself, so the password stays out of agent transcripts and tool logs.

Bad answers fail before anything is written: unknown

releases.name: DevSpace 1.1
releases.body:
DevSpace 1.1 turns DevSpace from a way to give ChatGPT and Claude access to your computer into a layer that also lets any of your coding agents hand work to the others. It's also much easier to install.

## Install in one command

```bash
curl -fsSL https://devspace.run/install | sh                          # macOS, Linux, WSL
powershell -c "irm https://devspace.run/install.ps1 | iex"            # Windows
```

The installer uses a compatible Node on your `PATH` or downloads Node 24 LTS just for DevSpace, installs without `sudo`, puts `devspace` on your `PATH`, and starts setup. Rerun it any time to update. Nothing is compiled during install anymore: state now uses Node's built-in SQLite, and terminal sessions use prebuilt binaries on every platform. `npm install -g @waishnav/devspace` still works if you manage Node yourself.

## Subagents for every coding agent

`devspace agents` runs Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Pi, Cursor, Copilot, Grok, or any ACP agent as a subagent, from ChatGPT, Claude, another coding agent, or your own shell. No server is needed for the CLI.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A self-hosted MCP server bringing Codex-style local coding workflows securely to ChatGPT and Claude Web.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: DevSpace is a self-hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that lets cloud-based AI assistants read, edit, search, and run code directly in your local projects. It establishes a secure, password-protected reverse tunnel connection between agents like ChatGPT and your machine without uploading files to a third party. The server provides isolated access to approved workspaces and local terminal environments, effectively turning the browser into a powerful local coding agent. It enables robust automated workflows including test execution, build management, and independent Git worktree editing while maintaining strict access controls.
keyFeatures: Local Code Execution: Gives AI agents the explicit ability to read files, write code, and run shell commands directly on your local machine.
Secure Reverse Tunneling: Connects securely using standard proxy tools like Cloudflare Tunnel or ngrok protected by a dedicated Owner password.
MCP Protocol Support: Fully implements the Model Context Protocol to serve as a standard custom application connector for modern LLM clients.
Isolated Git Workspaces: Supports utilizing Git worktrees for parallel AI coding sessions without inadvertently impacting your main branch.
Skill Discovery: Automatically detects and integrates local agent skills defined within your project's AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md files.

useCases.title: AI-Assisted Local Development
useCases.description: Provide ChatGPT direct access to your local repository to autonomously write code, run test suites, and debug errors in real-time.

useCases.title: Secure Enterprise Automation
useCases.description: Leverage powerful cloud LLMs for local development tasks without violating data privacy policies that forbid sending codebase files to external servers.

useCases.title: Parallel Branch Editing
useCases.description: Allow an AI agent to work and test features in an isolated Git worktree simultaneously while you continue coding on the main branch.

useCases.title: Automated Build Management
useCases.description: Instruct an AI assistant to automatically execute package scripts, trigger builds, and manage complex terminal workflows directly.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Software developers and engineers looking to deeply integrate powerful cloud AI assistants into their local development environment securely. Familiarity with agent-orchestration workflows is highly recommended for optimal usage.
